maternal diabetes is associated with a lower iron stores at birth in infants born to women with diabetes mellitis.

the study of the iron status of neonates born to diabetic mothers.
the effect of maternal DM on the iron status of neonates.
the study of iron metabolism in diabetic pregnancy and the effect of diabetes on fetal iron status.

iron deficiency anemia in the neonate is more common in diabetic mothers than in non-diabetic ones.
the iron status of newborns of diabetic mothers was significantly lower than those born to non-diabetics.
maternal diabetes mellitus has a significant effect on fetal iron status and this is reflected by the lower cord blood ferritin levels and higher transferrin receptor levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the iron status of neonate of the diabetic mothers is significantly lower than the non-diabetic mothers.
maternal diabetes mellitus is associated with depletion of the fetal iron stores in the neonate.
maternal diabetes mellitus is associated with depletion of neonatal cord blood ferritin and increase in serum transferrin receptors levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maternal iron supplementation does not improve fetal iron status in diabetic women.
iron status in the fetus is affected by maternal diabetes and that this is not related to maternal serum iron levels or to maternal glycemic control.
maternal diabetes mellitus is associated with lower iron stores at birth.
